newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Red October plans Eurobond.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Red October plans Eurobond.

text.p: Russia's biggest confectioner Red October plans to issue a Eurobond this autumn or winter, the company's chief economist Yuri Yegorov said on Monday.
"The placement is scheduled for the last third of 1997 in Europe under English law," Yegorov told a news conference.
He said OAO Konditerskaya Fabrika Krasny Oktyabr planned to raise about the same amount of funds as it planned from preferred shares issue this year.
Red October plans to sell about 1.48 million preferred shares with a face value of 1,000 roubles at 75-80 percent of the market value of ordinary shares at the time of placement.
Red October was last traded on April 11 on the Russian Trading System, at $20.00, putting a value of about $22 million on the entire issue.
Funds from Eurobond and shares sales will be used to buy new equipment, said Red October president Anatoly Daursky. Sixty percent of the company's equipment is outdated, he said.
